voice.question: Has he shipped real-time voice?
voice.answer: Yes. He built Hireanex's real-time voice engine: streaming speech-to-text, LLM reasoning and streaming text-to-speech, with voice activity detection and barge-in (interruption) handling. It is live with real users and pilot customers.

evidence.question: How are AI scores made trustworthy?
evidence.answer: Every score Hireanex produces is tied to quotes from the interview transcript. The LLM evaluation layer has to show its evidence, so each hiring decision is explainable and auditable.

models.question: Does he fine-tune models?
models.answer: Yes. He fine-tunes open-source models with LoRA on GPU infrastructure (PyTorch, Hugging Face, CUDA) and serves them with vLLM for faster, cheaper inference.

infra.question: What's under the AI: infra?
infra.answer: A Node/Fastify + PostgreSQL backend with REST and WebSocket APIs, BullMQ queues with idempotent workers (audio -> transcript -> evidence -> scores), all running on AWS with Docker, Kubernetes and Terraform, plus CI/CD, tests and observability. Before Hireanex he spent three years at Zingaro AI moving services to Kubernetes across 5+ environments and cutting cloud costs by 15%+.

fde.question: What does forward deployed mean for him?
fde.answer: He works directly with Hireanex's pilot customers: gathering requirements, integrating the platform into their hiring workflows, and turning their feedback into shipped features within days.

workflow.question: How does he use AI to build?
workflow.answer: AI-native. Claude Code, Codex and MCP agents act as his engineering team. He owns the architecture, writes the specs and reviews every change. Software engineer first: AI is how he builds, not a substitute for engineering.
